Clinical_Summary: 24yo, no symptoms, no history, non-smoker, BMI 22, not planning children
Clinical_Rationale: Zero risk factors and no conception delay warrant routine preventive self-care.

Clinical_Summary: 29yo, smoker, BMI 32, not planning children
Clinical_Rationale: Combined obesity (2 pts) and tobacco use (1 pt) reach Medium band (3 pts) for primary care metabolic/lifestyle review.

Clinical_Summary: 33yo, trying to conceive for 14 months, no other history
Clinical_Rationale: EAU/ASRM guidelines recommend couple fertility evaluation and semen analysis after >=12 months of unprotected intercourse.

Clinical_Summary: 36yo, trying 7 months, partner aged 37
Clinical_Rationale: When the female partner is >=35 years old, ASRM/EAU guidelines lower the evaluation threshold to >=6 months of trying.

Clinical_Summary: 31yo, trying 5 months, partner under 35, no history
Clinical_Rationale: Trying <6 months with no risk factors is within normal conception timelines; provide preconception self-care advice.

Clinical_Summary: 22yo, sudden severe left testicular pain since this morning
Clinical_Rationale: Acute severe testicular pain is suspected testicular torsion until proven otherwise and requires emergency surgical evaluation within hours.

Clinical_Summary: 40yo, new hard painless lump found on testicle while showering
Clinical_Rationale: A new intrascrotal mass or hardness requires prompt urological assessment and scrotal ultrasound within days to rule out testicular malignancy.

Clinical_Summary: 27yo, childhood history of undescended testis (orchidopexy), no symptoms
Clinical_Rationale: Prior cryptorchidism carries a major long-term risk of impaired spermatogenesis and warrants baseline specialist andrology review.

Clinical_Summary: 35yo, previous abnormal semen analysis report
Clinical_Rationale: Established abnormal semen parameters require targeted andrological workup and repeat confirmatory WHO laboratory testing.

Clinical_Summary: 30yo, exogenous testosterone and anabolic steroid use for 2 years, planning children within a year
Clinical_Rationale: Exogenous androgens suppress the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis causing severe oligo/azoospermia requiring specialist cessation management.

Clinical_Summary: 28yo, fever with painful swollen scrotum for 2 days
Clinical_Rationale: Acute febrile scrotal swelling suggests severe epididymo-orchitis or abscess requiring immediate emergency evaluation.

Clinical_Summary: 45yo, type 2 diabetes and erectile difficulty, not planning children
Clinical_Rationale: Co-existing diabetes and erectile dysfunction warrant primary care cardiovascular, glycemic, and hormonal evaluation.

Clinical_Summary: 26yo, history of incompletely treated urogenital STI, no current acute pain
Clinical_Rationale: Untreated or incompletely treated urogenital infection requires primary care NAAT screening and antimicrobial clearance to prevent obstruction.

Clinical_Summary: 17yo adolescent attempting intake with consent checked
Clinical_Rationale: Tool scope is restricted to consenting adults aged 18 and over; minors stop at gate R0 with zero data stored.

Clinical_Summary: 34yo adult who declines the initial privacy consent gate
Clinical_Rationale: Explicit consent is mandatory before processing any reproductive health inputs.

Clinical_Summary: 31yo with painful erection lasting >4 hours (priapism)
Clinical_Rationale: Ischemic priapism (>4 hours) is a urological emergency requiring immediate corporal aspiration to prevent permanent fibrosis.

Clinical_Summary: 25yo with blunt groin trauma during football followed by acute scrotal swelling
Clinical_Rationale: Traumatic scrotal swelling requires emergency ultrasound to exclude testicular rupture or intratesticular hematoma.

Clinical_Summary: 38yo with acute scrotal swelling (D2) AND prior abnormal semen test (B1) and trying 18m
Clinical_Rationale: Emergency red flags (R1) always override chronic specialist (R3) and fertility (R4) rules.

Clinical_Summary: 29yo with sudden severe testicular pain (D1) and new lump (D5)
Clinical_Rationale: Immediate emergency care (R1) takes strict precedence over fast-track urgent urology (R2).

Clinical_Summary: 37yo noticing blood in semen (hematospermia) and persistent scrotal ache for 3 weeks
Clinical_Rationale: Persistent scrotal pain >2 weeks or hematospermia warrants prompt outpatient urological workup.

Clinical_Summary: 34yo with new testicular lump (D5) who has also been trying to conceive for 16 months
Clinical_Rationale: Ruling out testicular neoplasia (R2) takes priority over routine fertility clinic referral (R4).

Clinical_Summary: 42yo with persistent scrotal heaviness (D6) and known varicocele (B5)
Clinical_Rationale: Symptomatic ache >2 weeks (R2) upgrades a routine varicocele (R5) to prompt urological assessment.

Clinical_Summary: 29yo lymphoma survivor treated with chemotherapy 3 years ago, planning children soon
Clinical_Rationale: Prior gonadotoxic chemotherapy requires specialist andrology evaluation for post-treatment spermatogenic recovery.

Clinical_Summary: 32yo diagnosed with Klinefelter syndrome / Y-chromosome microdeletion (B7)
Clinical_Rationale: Known genetic or chromosomal conditions affecting fertility require specialist andrology and reproductive genetics care.

Clinical_Summary: 36yo with prior chemotherapy (B6) AND trying to conceive for 15 months
Clinical_Rationale: Established gonadotoxic history (R3) routes directly to specialist andrology ahead of general fertility intake (R4).

Clinical_Summary: 30yo trying to conceive for exactly 12 months, partner aged 28, no other risk factors
Clinical_Rationale: Exact 12-month boundary triggers standard couple fertility and semen evaluation.

Clinical_Summary: 34yo trying to conceive for exactly 6 months, partner aged 36, no other risk factors
Clinical_Rationale: Exact 6-month boundary with partner >=35 triggers earlier fertility workup.

Clinical_Summary: 34yo trying to conceive for 6 months, partner aged 31 (under 35), no other risk factors
Clinical_Rationale: At 6 months with a partner under 35 and zero risk factors, premature fertility referral is avoided.

Clinical_Summary: 28yo with clinically diagnosed varicocele (B5), asymptomatic, planning children within a year
Clinical_Rationale: Known varicocele in a man planning conception warrants routine urology/andrology assessment and baseline semen analysis.

Clinical_Summary: 39yo with mumps orchitis history (B3), groin surgery (B4), and diabetes (C2) -> Score 6 (High)
Clinical_Rationale: Cumulative multi-factor burden of 3 Moderate factors (6 points = High band) warrants specialist andrology review.

Clinical_Summary: 33yo with varicocele (B5 = Major) and erectile difficulty (D7 = 2 pts) -> Score 5 bumped to High band
Clinical_Rationale: A Major factor combined with sexual dysfunction forces High band and specialist routing.

Clinical_Summary: 35yo with childhood groin surgery (B4=2), BMI 33 (C1=2), tobacco (C3=1), heavy alcohol (C4=1) -> Score 6
Clinical_Rationale: Surgical history plus severe modifiable metabolic/lifestyle clustering (6 pts = High) routes to specialist care.

Clinical_Summary: 27yo taking finasteride for hair loss (C10=True), no other risk factors (Score 0)
Clinical_Rationale: Fertility-relevant medications require primary care review with an explicit warning never to stop medicine without doctor advice.

Clinical_Summary: 41yo with well-controlled diabetes (C2=True), BMI 24, non-smoker (Score 2, Band Low)
Clinical_Rationale: Diabetes alone (even in Low score band) explicitly routes to primary care for metabolic and reproductive check-up.

Clinical_Summary: 36yo with isolated erectile/ejaculatory concern (D7=True), no other history (Score 2, Band Low)
Clinical_Rationale: Sexual function concerns route to primary care for morning testosterone, metabolic screening, and targeted support.

Clinical_Summary: 31yo baker with groin heat exposure (C7=1), chemical exposure (C8=1), and recent high fever (C9=1) -> Score 3
Clinical_Rationale: Three minor occupational/transient exposures sum to 3 points (Medium band), warranting primary care guidance and repeat check after 74 days.

Clinical_Summary: 29yo who skips 7 of 19 triage questions (>30% missing) with zero positive answers
Clinical_Rationale: Skipping >30% of non-safety triage questions triggers the low-confidence flag and bumps Low band to Medium (R6).

Clinical_Summary: 26yo smoker (C3=1) who drinks regularly (8-14/wk, C4='regular'=0), BMI 24 -> Score 1
Clinical_Rationale: A single minor modifiable factor (Score 1, Low band) receives targeted smoking cessation and preconception self-care advice.

Clinical_Summary: 32yo with BMI 30.5 (C1=2) and zero other risk factors -> Score 2 (Low band)
Clinical_Rationale: Isolated mild obesity (2 pts, Low band) without diabetes or subfertility receives actionable weight and metabolic self-care guidance.

Clinical_Summary: 25yo healthy man who selects 'prefer not to say' (None) on acute pain D1
Clinical_Rationale: Prefer-not-to-say on a red flag never triggers a false emergency, but activates the explicit safety-net warning on the result screen.

Clinical_Summary: Adult user with missing age (age=None) despite checking consent
Clinical_Rationale: Age verification is required to confirm adult eligibility before screening.

Clinical_Summary: 16yo user with acute testicular pain who attempts to use adult tool
Clinical_Rationale: Hard consent/age gate R0 executes first and directs underage users out of adult intake with emergency disclaimer.

Clinical_Summary: 21yo with sudden scrotal swelling and redness (D2) starting 6 hours ago
Clinical_Rationale: Isolated sudden scrotal swelling/inflammation requires immediate emergency evaluation.

Clinical_Summary: 30yo with fever plus testicular pain (D3) and untreated STI history (B8)
Clinical_Rationale: Acute febrile orchitis/epididymitis (R1) overrides routine STI primary care (R6).

Clinical_Summary: 27yo bodybuilder on steroids (C5) presenting with prolonged erection >4h (D4)
Clinical_Rationale: Acute priapism emergency (R1) overrides routine andrology steroid referral (R5).

Clinical_Summary: 33yo with painless testicular size change (D5) and childhood undescended testis (B2)
Clinical_Rationale: Cryptorchidism increases testicular cancer risk; a new size change requires fast-track R2 urgent urology over routine R5.

Clinical_Summary: 44yo with blood in semen (D6) taking fertility-relevant prescription medication (C10)
Clinical_Rationale: Urgent assessment for hematospermia (R2) takes priority over primary care medication review (R6) while preserving the medicine note.

Clinical_Summary: 31yo with prior abnormal semen test (B1) and trying for 8 months with 36yo partner (R4 also true)
Clinical_Rationale: When a man already has a known abnormal semen test (R3), direct andrology/urology evaluation supersedes general fertility intake (R4).

Clinical_Summary: 28yo with chromosomal microdeletion (B7) and varicocele (B5)
Clinical_Rationale: Established genetic etiology (R3) takes precedence over routine varicocele rule (R5).

Clinical_Rationale: At 11 months with a partner under 35 and zero risk factors, the 12-month R4 threshold is not yet met.

Clinical_Summary: 40yo trying for 15 months with partner under 35, also has diabetes (C2) and smokes (C3)
Clinical_Rationale: Couple conception delay >=12 months (R4) takes precedence over primary care metabolic routing (R6).

Clinical_Summary: 35yo with childhood undescended testis (B2=3) and erectile difficulty (D7=2) -> High band
Clinical_Rationale: Undescended testis plus sexual dysfunction triggers High band and specialist andrology evaluation.

Clinical_Rationale: High cumulative score (6 pts) from historical plus modifiable factors routes to routine andrology/urology.

Clinical_Summary: 34yo with mumps orchitis (B3=2) and regular sauna/groin heat exposure (C7=1) -> Score 3
Clinical_Rationale: Moderate history (2 pts) plus minor modifiable heat exposure (1 pt) reaches Medium band (3 pts) for primary care evaluation.

Clinical_Summary: 38yo with prior inguinal hernia repair (B4=2) and occupational chemical exposure (C8=1) -> Score 3
Clinical_Rationale: Prior groin surgery combined with occupational toxin exposure reaches Medium band (R6) to order baseline semen analysis.

Clinical_Summary: 31yo with BMI 31 (C1=2, Low band) who skips 6 of 19 triage questions (>30% missing) -> bumped to Medium
Clinical_Rationale: Low-confidence missingness (>30% skipped) bumps a borderline Low score (2 pts) into Medium band (R6).

Clinical_Summary: 29yo with childhood mumps orchitis (B3=2) only, no other risk factors, not trying
Clinical_Rationale: A single isolated Moderate history factor (2 pts = Low band) without trying delay stays in preventive self-care.

Clinical_Summary: 33yo with BMI 29.9 (just below obesity cutoff) and occasional alcohol (1-7/wk) -> Score 0
Clinical_Rationale: Sub-threshold overweight BMI (<30) and occasional alcohol score 0 points and receive preventive lifestyle tips.

Clinical_Rationale: Skipping <=30% of questions does not trigger a low-confidence bump; transient recent fever (1 pt) receives self-care & re-test timing note.
